Changelog

What changed, and when

This is curated from the repository's own history. Releases are listed newest first. The current release is 4.9.0, and the entry above it is work on main that has not been cut into a release yet.

  1. 4.9.0 · 2026-10-21

    A bot is a bot, and not the developer who made it

    • Added — a bot is a bot, and not the developer who made it

  2. 4.8.0 · 2026-10-21

    The relay answers where the clients are given, and a picture is a picture

    • Added — the relay answers where the clients are given, and a picture is a picture

  3. 4.7.0 · 2026-10-21

    One table of what can be done to a thing, and the truth in the voice console

    • Added — one table of what can be done to a thing, and the truth in the voice console

  4. 4.6.0 · 2026-10-21

    The mesh is turnkey, and the relay answers where a client can reach it

    • Added — the mesh is turnkey, and the relay answers where a client can reach it

  5. 4.5.0 · 2026-10-21

    The sidebar glides, the layers are one band, and the browser harness stops lying

    • Added — the sidebar glides, and the browser harness stops lying

  6. 4.4.0 · 2026-10-21

    The community's own rules, its notes, and what its members may do

    • Added — a community's rules, its notes, and what its members may do

  7. 4.3.0 · 2026-10-21

    A message can be swiped to reply to

    • Added — a message can be swiped to reply to

  8. 4.2.0 · 2026-10-21

    The gates in two panes, and the instance on the form

    • Added — the gates are in two panes, with the instance named on the form

  9. 4.1.2 · 2026-10-21

    The gates have two panes, and the sign-in says which instance

    • Added — the gates are in two panes, with the instance named
    • Fixed — the null was still printed, because the rule was put on an object nothing calls
    • Fixed — the sign-in did not say which instance a reader was signing in to

  10. 4.0.3 · 2026-10-21

    The extension surface is a range

    • Fixed — the extension surface was one number, and only a package built against the running release installed
    • Fixed — the phone never showed the roles of a person in a community
    • Fixed — a preview image had no space reserved, so the message jumped when it arrived

  11. 4.0.0 · 2026-10-21

    The sidebar could be tapped, and nothing printed null

    • Fixed — the sidebar was drawn under the scrim, so none of its links could be pressed
    • Fixed — a page that rendered a conditional printed the word null where there was nothing
    • Fixed — a reader could not sign in with the address they were given
    • Added — an operator can set a password and clear a second factor from the host

  12. 3.9.0 · 2026-10-21

    Every route measured, and a profile that says who somebody is

    • Fixed — the control that creates a channel was twenty pixels square
    • Fixed — the way back on the public pages was forty pixels tall
    • Fixed — a segmented item was a pixel short of a finger
    • Fixed — the profile said Profile rather than the name of the person
    • Fixed — the profile said the date of the membership twice
    • Added — the profile can be written to, and the roles are chips in their colours

  13. 3.8.0 · 2026-10-21

    A conversation of more than two people

    • Added — a conversation of more than two people: it has a name, it can be started, and it can be changed

  14. 3.7.3 · 2026-10-21

    The communities that live on another instance, and a sweep of every route

    • Added — the communities that live on another instance are listed in a section of their own, with a page of their own
    • Fixed — the place column could not be drawn and said nothing about why
    • Fixed — the tests left a database behind every time they were interrupted
    • Fixed — the browser harness left its profile behind and filled the disk

  15. 3.6.20 · 2026-10-20

    The roles in their colours, and a harness that measures this product

    • Fixed — the role colours were never drawn, because no rule read the colour
    • Fixed — the roster never showed the roles, because the row read a field the roster does not send
    • Fixed — the sheet about a person had no face, because the menu drew the header as a line of text
    • Fixed — a page printed the word null where a banner should have been
    • Fixed — the profile said Profile rather than the name of the person
    • Fixed — the stylesheet check did not look at the packages, so a class with no rule went unnoticed
    • Fixed — the quick paths said Direct instead of Direct messages
    • Fixed — the browser harness was measuring the deployed instance instead of the answers

  16. 3.6.12 · 2026-10-20

    The pictures, the previews, and the phone

    • Fixed — a picture that was replaced did not change, because the media cache was never emptied
    • Fixed — the picture was looked for under a different name on every surface, and the wrong one showed initials
    • Fixed — a link preview could be walked past, because the whole redirect chain was followed before anything was checked
    • Fixed — the name was resolved twice, so a short-lived answer could pass the check and fail the connection
    • Fixed — the button on the phone was 40 pixels and the mark in the app bar was 28
    • Fixed — the harness was measuring a sign-in page and never read the errors it was shown

  17. 3.6.6 · 2026-10-20

    Six faults, found by running the suites

    • Fixed — the enforcement actions on an account were refused, so the menu items did nothing
    • Fixed — every installed extension was broken, because the extension API version was the application version
    • Fixed — the voice console could not save anything, because it wrote through the page that refuses the voice settings
    • Fixed — the third-party SFU token belonged to no console, so it could not be set
    • Fixed — one setting was declared twice, so it was rendered twice and the second copy won
    • Fixed — the accessibility audit read a comment as code and reported a named button as unnamed

  18. 3.6.0 · 20 October 2026

    The voice stack that answers, the bots that listen, and the settings that have one owner

    • Fixed — the context menu closed when it was scrolled, and a closed menu left a handler behind that closed live menus.
    • Fixed — the poll editor threw on every click, so the whole poll surface was unreachable.
    • Fixed — removing your own picture threw, because the account settings called a function that was not in scope.
    • Fixed — the phone threw on a poll that had a voter, and on the poll editor.
    • Fixed — the instance answered every STUN request with nothing, because the encoder used a constant that was never defined and the handler threw the error away.
    • Fixed — the document editor refused a heading written with a single hash, and accused the writer of using two or three.
    • Fixed — the place column disappeared at 125% zoom, because the width it turned at was a laptop width and not a phone width.
    • Fixed — the registration form had no place to accept the documents, and the button said nothing about why it was closed.
    • Fixed — the voice settings could be changed in two places at once, and the two could disagree.
    • Fixed — the instance directory did not exist, and the register page linked to it.
    • Fixed — the community settings mount swallowed the route a reader uses to join a community.
    • Added — the voice subsystem is a process of its own, with its own health and its own diagnostics.
    • Added — an application can listen: the gateway hands a bot the same events a webhook is handed.
    • Added — community onboarding: the welcome, the rules, and the questions, and what an answer does.
    • Added — the instance directory is a page of the public site.
    • Added — the workspace uses the width it is given, and the card head stops clipping its button.
    • Added — the client and the backend are checked for the names they use and do not have.
    • The sign-in and registration pages now stand alone. The shell that was meant to hide was not hiding: a component that sets its own display beats the browser's rule for the hidden attribute, so the empty shell kept the viewport and pushed the page below it.
    • The demo and the community directory reach the instance again. The public site and the API are different origins in a real deployment, and the pages were asking for a relative path that the site cannot answer; they now resolve the address the same way the application does.
    • The deployment build was shipping an old tree: it fetched the newest source and then checked out the branch it already had. It now deploys what it fetched.
    • Instance discovery, per-instance sessions, an in-house search index, backups with a restore path, housekeeping, and one honest report per subsystem all land in this release.
    • The version is reported by the server, the API and the application, and all of them say the same thing.

  19. 2.5.0 · 19 October 2026

    One backend, a chosen instance, and a machine that is not fighting itself

    • The backend was consolidated on backend/: the features and tables that lived only in the legacy server/ package were merged in, and a production instance now runs one backend instead of the split that had drifted.
    • The application was put on the canonical asset library: one generated set of design tokens that the app, the themes and the website all read.
    • A configuration centre was added where every setting shown actually does something, and mail gained a provider registry with an admin console.
    • Registration approval was added, with the migration parity check that had been missing.
    • Realtime naming was made consistent across the gateway and the client, kept in agreement by a check rather than by discipline.
    • This public site was rebuilt as its own composition, with a working demo and a public community directory, instead of a smaller copy of the app's layout.
    • Registration now takes an instance: browse the instances an instance knows about, or give the address of one you run. The address is checked against that instance before it is accepted, and a session belongs to the instance that issued it, so switching never carries a token across.
    • Search became an in-house index that works on every database this runs on, and the permission check lives inside it: a message from a community you are not in cannot answer a query.
    • Backups can be taken from the administration page and put back with a command that verifies the dump first and asks for the database name before it replaces anything.
    • The administration pages grew a rail, so every settings door and every moderation queue is one click away, and a diagnostics page that reports each subsystem as it really is rather than as its configuration implies.
    • The voice path is the in-house one, and an administrator's saved choice is what takes effect: the provider used to be read from the environment, which meant a setting that saved and changed nothing.
    • Housekeeping came with the jobs: expired sessions, old notifications and finished work are cleaned up on a rhythm that survives a restart.
    • The automated check suite was removed. It booted whole instances and started browsers, and on a small host it was more load than the product was worth; verification is now a real journey against a running instance.
    • Plain-language passes on error messages, settings and navigation.

  20. 1.6.4 · 3 October 2026

    Attachments, replies, and a release step that runs anywhere

    • Attachments in direct messages as well as communities, a tray you can see and undo, and a full-screen lightbox.
    • Replies, with a badge that follows the message it answers.
    • Rich link previews with a per-message opt-out, and an endpoint that declares its arguments instead of guessing.
    • Embeds, analytics and webhooks, and bot applications, behind a single permission gate.
    • The client is told its own server: a self-hosted instance stops advertising someone else's backend, and the server can find the client next to itself.
    • Release verification moved to bash so it runs on every platform, and the browser checks were brought into the repository.

  21. 1.6.3 · 27 September 2026

    One seeded role, and the owner inherits everything

    • @everyone is the only seeded role and the community baseline. The owner inherits every permission from ownership rather than from a role, so no Admin or Moderator roles are created for them.
    • Fixed a bug that made the baseline role unconfigurable, and removed self-assignable roles end to end.
    • Context menus added for notifications, friends, invites and search results.
    • The render-crash watchdog no longer mistakes a valid sign-in screen for a hang, and the desktop app gained CORS diagnostics for its own scheme.

  22. 1.6.2 · 26 September 2026

    Contextual navigation and a full-width workspace

    • Navigation rebuilt around contextual shells: a home sidebar and a menu page, with the mobile drawer removed.
    • The workspace layout rebuilt around a full-width chat view, with loading and empty states and a hover bar.
    • A theme system overhaul, including a client that heals itself instead of rendering a blank window when a render crashes.
    • One uniform template across every static public page.

  23. 1.6.1 · 25 September 2026

    Desktop publishing and the portable build

    • Desktop builds published to the project repository, with the portable Windows build named TrycordPTB.

  24. 1.6.0 and 1.5.0 · 23 September 2026

    Themes, and the design system reconciled

    • A seven-theme ecosystem: token-override themes and a custom palette derivation.
    • The appearance interface with persistence, and the theme restored at boot.
    • The written design system was reconciled with the code so the two could not quietly disagree.

  25. 1.0.1 · 20 September 2026

    No more blank page on an updated client

    • The server never serves a stale client bundle; it shows a reload notice instead of a blank page.

  26. 0.5.0 · 19 September 2026

    Self-hosting, and a configurable database

    • The client serve path, runtime configuration, and instance state.
    • MySQL and SQLite adapters behind one interface, with a validated boot.
    • CORS origins and the /api/instance endpoint other client work depends on.

For the commit-level record, the repository history is the source this page is drawn from. Releases are published on GitHub.
